newsitem.title: USA: Chattanooga, Tenn., plans conference center.
newsitem.headline: Chattanooga, Tenn., plans conference center.

text.p: Chattanooga, Tenn., will launch a revitalization of its Southside district with construction of a trade center and a conference center next year, Mayor Jon Kinsey said Thursday.
The city plans to issue bonds for the projects in early 1998, Kinsey said.
Cost of the two projects is estimated at $50 million. Kinsey said the city and private interests are expected to pump hundreds of millions of dollars into the area over 10 to 15 years.

"The Southside is going to be a model area for our city where people can work and live and worship. There's a lot of churches, a school is planned for the area. Unlike past redevelopment where they came in and bulldozed everything, we're going to take what is there and work with it," Kinsey said.

The city passed a half-cent sales tax increase last year to provide funds for initial construction. The tax is expected to raise about $13 million a year, with half allocated for schools and half earmarked for economic development.
The city council approved plans for the project 5-1 on Tuesday.
